paper_title: On the Complexity of Locally Dense Lattices
classifications: Theory of computation → Computational complexity and cryptography
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 5
statement: Our main result shows that (p, α)-LDLP is Πp2 -complete for every finite p ≥ log2 3 and every α ∈ (2−1/p , 1). It remains open whether the same holds for every 1 ≤ p < log2 3 and every α ∈ (2−1/p , 1). The obstacle in our proof is the step that forces sufficiently short vectors in Wan’s shifted coset to be Boolean. Regev and Rosen [31] gave randomized reductions between lattice problems in different ℓp norms using embeddings between normed spaces. Since our hardness result includes the Euclidean norm, it is natural to ask whether their reductions can be combined with our construction to obtain hardness of LDLP under randomized reductions for every p ≥ 1.
context: 1.4 Open problems Our main result shows that (p, α)-LDLP is Πp2 -complete for every finite p ≥ log2 3 and every α ∈ (2−1/p , 1). It remains open whether the same holds for every 1 ≤ p < log2 3 and every α ∈ (2−1/p , 1). The obstacle in our proof is the step that forces sufficiently short vectors in Wan’s shifted coset to be Boolean. Regev and Rosen [31] gave randomized reductions between lattice problems in different ℓp norms using embeddings between normed spaces. Since our hardness result includes the Euclidean norm, it is natural to ask whether their reductions can be combined with our construction to obtain hardness of LDLP under randomized reductions for every p ≥ 1. There is an analogous recognition problem for codes. Locally dense codes have been used in hardness results for MDP [14, 11, 29, 2]. It would be interesting to determine whether recognizing locally dense codes is also Πp2 -complete. The quantifier structure of LDLP is related to the CRP. Haviv and Regev [18] proved Πp2 - hardness of approximation for the lattice version in large ℓp norms. An interesting question is whether similar techniques can prove Πp2 -hardness for the Euclidean lattice version.
